svg.title: How much weight the posterior mean gives the data as the sample grows
svg.desc: Left panel: two rising curves showing the weight on the data against sample size, one for a prior worth ten trials and one for a prior worth four observations. Right panel: the posterior mean climbing from 0.20 toward 0.30.
svg.text: A posterior mean is a weighted average, and the weights move with n
Weight the posterior mean puts on the data
so at n = 30 the weight is 0.75
so at n = 16 the weight is 0.80
weight one, where the prior stops mattering
Where the posterior mean sits, if the rate stays 0.30
A prior enters as a fixed number of pretend observations, so its share of the answer decays like one over n.
The data never win outright at any finite n, and the prior never loses outright either.
